summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag, a Slack-based feature that lets teams tag @Claude as a team member to delegate tasks, connect tools/data, and have it work asynchronously and proactively, replacing the existing Claude in Slack app.

mechanisms.reason: The lab reports its own internal deployment of tagging Claude to autonomously execute delegated tasks at measurable scale within the company.
mechanisms.quote: Today, 65% of our product team’s code is created by our internal version of Claude Tag.

mechanisms.reason: Delegating tasks to many parallel autonomous agents implies a higher volume of model calls per unit of work than single-chat usage.
mechanisms.quote: we now spend much more of our time delegating tasks to many Claudes in parallel.

practices.reason: Describes a concrete multi-agent, memory-persisting, asynchronous task-delegation pattern in Slack that a team could adapt, though the gain is only illustrated by internal anecdote rather than a controlled benchmark.
practices.quote: Tag @Claude with a request in simple terms and it’ll break its task down into stages and then work through them in turn, using the tools it has access to.

practices.reason: Existing Claude-in-Slack integrations must be migrated within a stated window, creating concrete integration work for teams using the prior app.
practices.quote: Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude in Slack app. To migrate, administrators can opt in within 30 days.
